dialogue.content: よろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: It's nice to meet you.

dialogue.content: (よろしくお願いいたします。11時より始めさせていただきます)
dialogue.English: (Nice to meet you. We will begin at 11:00.)

dialogue.content: はい！
dialogue.English: Yes!

dialogue.content: こんにちは、相談員です今日の相談にあたって、先ずあなたの年齢と性別、学生さんなのか社会人なのかを教えていただけますか？加えて、相談中にあなたのことを何とお呼びすればよろしいですか？
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm the counselor. Before we begin today's session, could you please tell me your age, gender, and whether you are a student or a working professional? Also, how would you like me to address you during our session?

dialogue.content: こんにちは。20代 女性 社会人「さなさん」でお願いします。
dialogue.English: Hello. I'm a woman in my 20s and a working professional. Please call me Sana-san.

dialogue.content: さなさんですね今日はどんなことを相談したいですか？
dialogue.English: Sana-san, is that right? What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 人に甘えたり、頼ることが苦手で、、、それが辛いんです。
dialogue.English: I have a hard time leaning on or relying on others... and it's causing me distress.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね...困りごとを一人で解決するのは大変な時もありますからお辛いですよね...
dialogue.English: I see... It can be really hard to solve problems on your own sometimes, so that must be painful for you...

dialogue.content: 職場でもプライベートでも、できなくて、、、最終的に悪い方向にいってしまうので、なんとかしないととおもうのですが、どうすればいいのかわからないんです。
dialogue.English: I can't do it at work or in my personal life... and things end up going badly. I feel I need to do something about it, but I don't know what to do.

dialogue.content: ずっと気を張っている?感じなのですね...助けがあれば良い結果に行ったであろうと思うこともあったのでしょうね...
dialogue.English: So it feels like you're always on edge? I imagine there have been times when you thought things would have turned out better if you'd had help.

dialogue.content: そうですね。気は張ってるとおもいます。職場の場合は、分からないことがあっても、先輩に聞くことで、できない子と思われるんぢゃないのかと思い、聞けれません。
dialogue.English: That's right. I think I am always on edge. At work, even if there's something I don't understand, I can't bring myself to ask a senior colleague because I'm afraid they'll think I'm incompetent.

dialogue.content: なるほど...たしかに自分の本心とは違った意味でとらえられてしまうのは悲しいですからね
dialogue.English: I understand... It's certainly sad to be perceived in a way that's different from your true intentions.

dialogue.content: わかりました今の状態から少しでも良くなるように、
dialogue.English: Understood. To help improve your current situation even a little,

dialogue.content: 昔のことを少しずつ思い返しながら、さなさんにとって少しでも良い可決策を時間いっぱいまで考えていければと思います
dialogue.English: I'd like to spend our time together thinking about the best possible solutions for you, while we gradually reflect on your past.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 出は先ず、さなさんは、どんな時に『甘えられてないな』『頼ることができなかったな』と感じますか？職場、プライベートどちらでも構いません
dialogue.English: Well then, first of all, in what kind of situations do you feel like, 'I'm not able to depend on others,' or 'I couldn't ask for help'? It can be at work or in your personal life.

dialogue.content: 職場の場合ですと、先程のように、分からないことが聞けないことですね。
dialogue.English: In the case of work, it's as I just mentioned: not being able to ask when I don't understand something.

dialogue.content: そうなんですねわからないことがあると困ってしまいますし、職場だと周りの影響にも気が向いてしまいますよね...さなさんは、どんなお仕事をしているのですか？
dialogue.English: I see. It's difficult when there's something you don't understand, and at work, you also have to be mindful of how it affects those around you... What kind of work do you do, Sana-san?

dialogue.content: 看護師をしています。忙しい職場なので、聞くのも気が引けますね
dialogue.English: I'm a nurse. It's a busy workplace, so I feel hesitant to ask questions.

dialogue.content: 看護師さんですかたしかに忙しくしている人に何か聞くのは躊躇してしまいますよね...
dialogue.English: You're a nurse? I can certainly understand why you'd hesitate to ask something of someone who is busy...

dialogue.content: はち
dialogue.English: Ye-

dialogue.content: 間違えました。
dialogue.English: Sorry, that was a mistake.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: キツめの人も多いし、聞きづらいですね
dialogue.English: There are a lot of stern people, too, which makes it hard to ask.

dialogue.content: 忙しいとピリピリしてしまう人もいますからね...例えば、さなさんは、どんな仕事の時に困ってしまいますか？守秘義務もあると思いますので、話せる範囲で大丈夫です
dialogue.English: Some people do get tense when they're busy... For example, what kind of tasks do you find difficult? I understand there are confidentiality obligations, so please only share what you're comfortable with.

dialogue.content: ん～具体的にこれといったものではなくて、全体的に。
dialogue.English: Hmm, it's not one specific thing, but more like everything in general.

dialogue.content: これなんだっけ？ってド忘れしてしまった事でも、恐怖で聞けないです
dialogue.English: Even when I just blank out and think, 'What was this again?' I'm too afraid to ask.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね...全般的となると都度都度確認したいこととかがでてくるのでしょうね...それだけでも辛いのに、怖くて聞けないというのも重なってすごく辛いですよね...
dialogue.English: I see... If it's in general, there must be things you want to confirm from time to time... That alone is tough, but to also be too scared to ask must make it doubly so. That sounds very distressing.

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: That's right.

dialogue.content: 「できない子」「頼りにならない」と思われるのはすごくいやで、自分で抱え込んでしまうんですよね
dialogue.English: I really hate being seen as 'incompetent' or 'unreliable,' so I just end up shouldering everything myself.

dialogue.content: 社会人1年目の時に、とにかく怖い先輩がいて、それがトラウマになってるのかもしれないです
dialogue.English: In my first year as a working adult, there was this senior colleague who was just terrifying, and that might have become a trauma for me.

dialogue.content: たしかに聞くことによってどう思われるかというのは気になってしまいますよね...期を張って、気疲れするのも当然です仕事も恐る恐る進めていくことになるので、とても不安な中のお仕事だと思います
dialogue.English: It's certainly understandable to worry about what others might think if you ask... It's natural to feel mentally exhausted from being on edge. You must have to do your work timidly, which I imagine makes you feel very anxious while working.

dialogue.content: はい。体力的よりも精神的に疲れますね。
dialogue.English: Yes. It's more mentally exhausting than physically.

dialogue.content: そうなってしまうのも当然だと思います今でも怖い先輩はいるのですが？
dialogue.English: That's completely understandable. Are there still intimidating seniors now?

dialogue.content: 病院も変わってるので、同じ先輩はいませんが、少し怖い人はいます
dialogue.English: I've changed hospitals, so that same person isn't here, but there are some people who are a bit intimidating.

dialogue.content: でも怖くない人に対しても、どう思われるのかが気になって、なかなか素が出せませんね
dialogue.English: But even with people who aren't scary, I worry about what they'll think of me, so I can't really be myself.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね...職場が変わってもそういう人はいるのですね...確かに環境が変わっても自分がどう思われているのかというの気になりますよね考えるだけで気疲れしそうな職場ですから大変ですよね...
dialogue.English: I see... So even at a different workplace, there are people like that... It's true that even in a new environment, you'd worry about how you're perceived. It sounds like a mentally taxing workplace just thinking about it; that must be difficult.

dialogue.content: はい、、
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: 気持ち的にもっと楽に仕事をしたい
dialogue.English: I want to feel more at ease mentally while working.

dialogue.content: わかりました先ずは、職場でもっと気疲れしないで仕事をできるような対策を考えていきましょう
dialogue.English: I understand. First, let's think about some strategies to help you work without feeling so mentally drained.

dialogue.content: はい、よろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you.

dialogue.content: さなさんは、昔からどちらかというと周りに何かを聴くときとかに気を使ってしまう感じだったのですか？
dialogue.English: Sana-san, have you always been the type to be very considerate of others when asking them something?

dialogue.content: あまり人には聞かずに自分で調べてたりしてたと思いますね
dialogue.English: I think I tended to look things up myself rather than ask people.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね自分で解決するというクセが身についているのかもしれませんね
dialogue.English: I see. You may have developed a habit of solving things on your own.

dialogue.content: たしかに。自分で何とかしようとしますね
dialogue.English: That's true. I do try to manage things myself.

dialogue.content: 当時、自分で調べて、それでも解決しなかった問題とかはどうされていましたか？
dialogue.English: Back then, what did you do about problems that you couldn't solve even after looking them up yourself?

dialogue.content: んー
dialogue.English: Hmm...

dialogue.content: 答えづらかった大丈夫ですよ
dialogue.English: It's okay if it's difficult to answer.

dialogue.content: そのまま時間が流れるのを待つか
dialogue.English: I'd either just wait for time to pass,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 聞きやすい人、外部の人に聞いてた気がします
dialogue.English: or I'd ask someone who was easier to talk to—someone external.

dialogue.content: なるほど当時聞きやすい人というと、友人とか家族とかですか？
dialogue.English: I see. When you say someone easy to talk to back then, do you mean friends or family?

dialogue.content: そうですね
dialogue.English: That's right.

dialogue.content: その時には、快く助けてもらえましたか？
dialogue.English: And when you did, were they happy to help you?

dialogue.content: 半々ですね！
dialogue.English: It was about half and half!

dialogue.content: 悩みを打ち明けて反対されることもありました
dialogue.English: There were times I'd open up about my worries and they'd disagree with me.

dialogue.content: でもその時は結局自分のことを信じて、自分の思うようにいきました
dialogue.English: But in those moments, I ended up believing in myself and did what I thought was right.

dialogue.content: そうなんですねさなさん一人で解決できなかった問題を半分も解決することができたんですね相談した結果、自分の思いをより強く持つという効果もあったようで、プラスの影響はあったのではないかなと感じたのですがいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. So you were able to solve half of the problems you couldn't handle on your own. It seems that as a result of consulting others, it also had the effect of strengthening your own convictions. I feel that was a positive influence, what do you think?

dialogue.content: たしかにそうかもしれないですね
dialogue.English: Yes, that might be true.

dialogue.content: 今の職場では、そんな昔みたいに相談しやすい人はどのぐらいいます？
dialogue.English: At your current workplace, how many people are there who are easy to talk to like that?

dialogue.content: 別の部署なので一緒には仕事をしませんが1人います
dialogue.English: There's one person, though they're in a different department so we don't work together.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね部署が違うと仕事の内容も結構違うものなのですか？残り時間が15分前になりましたが、時間いっぱいまでお話を聞かせてください
dialogue.English: I see. Is the work quite different in other departments? We have about 15 minutes left, but please feel free to talk until our time is up.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。仕事の内容は違いますね。
dialogue.English: Thank you. Yes, the work itself is different.

dialogue.content: なんか、直接関係のない人には頼れるのに、当人には頼れないんですよね、、、、
dialogue.English: For some reason, I can rely on people who aren't directly involved, but I can't rely on the actual people concerned...

dialogue.content: そうなんですね直接的な解決にはならないかもしれませんが、それでも相談をしてみるというのはいかがですか？言葉にして吐き出すだけでも、精神的に楽になるという効果はありますので
dialogue.English: I see. It might not lead to a direct solution, but how about trying to consult with them anyway? Just putting your feelings into words and getting them out can have the effect of easing your mental burden.

dialogue.content: そうですね。その方にはいろいろ話は聞いていただいてるんです。
dialogue.English: That's right. That person does listen to me about various things.

dialogue.content: 精神的には楽になりますが、その場に戻ると結局同じことの繰り返しなんですよね、、、、
dialogue.English: It does make me feel better mentally, but when I return to the situation, it ends up being the same cycle again...

dialogue.content: 確かに、関係ないからこそ話せるということはありますよねそうだったんですねとてもいいことだと思いますもう少し、そのような相談を増やしていってもいいのかもしれませんねその分相手の相談にも乗ってあげるという感じで
dialogue.English: Indeed, sometimes it's easier to talk precisely because they're not directly involved. I see—that's a very good thing. It might help to increase those kinds of conversations a bit more, and in return you could also listen to them when they need to talk.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 確かに職場環境的には解決には至らないかもしれませんねその問題の具体的な解決策が見つかるまでは、いったん精神的な負担を軽減する対策をするという方向で考えていくというのはいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: You're right, it might not resolve the workplace situation itself. Until we find a specific solution to that problem, how about we focus on measures to reduce your mental burden for now?

dialogue.content: 具体的な解決策をみつけるためには何をしたらいいのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: What should I do to find a concrete solution?

dialogue.content: そうですね...今の時点ではすぐに答えは出ませんが、周囲の状況や考え方を変えていくことは難しいので、さなさんに負担にならないような部分で仕事の何かを変えていくという手段がいいと思います
dialogue.English: Let's see... We won't find an answer right away, but since it's difficult to change the circumstances or the way people around you think, I think a good approach would be to change something about your work in a way that doesn't burden you.

dialogue.content: 仕事の何か、、、、
dialogue.English: Something about my work...

dialogue.content: 例えば、ド忘れしそうな時があれば、小さなメモを常に持ち歩いておいて、サッと取り出してかけるようにしておくなど...引き続きお仕事の状況を聞きながら一緒に考えていきましょう
dialogue.English: For example, if you think you might blank on something, carry a small memo pad so you can pull it out quickly and jot things down... Let's keep talking about your work situation and think this through together.

dialogue.content: 分かりました
dialogue.English: I understand.

dialogue.content: さなさんの今の問題を少しまとめます
dialogue.English: Let me summarize your current issues a bit, Sana-san.

dialogue.content: はち
dialogue.English: Ah.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 今の職場で少しでも楽に仕事ができるようになりたい特に精神的に負担がかかっている問題としては、困ったときに人に聴ける状況になく、不安の中で仕事していて、とても辛い相談できる人も部署が違い、具体的な解決策もなかなか出てこない大まかに環境的なストレスと、精神的なストレスと大きく二つに分けるられ、先ずは精神的な負担を減らしながら、より具体的な解決策を考えていく
dialogue.English: You want to be able to work more comfortably at your current job. The issue causing particular mental strain is that you're not in a situation where you can ask people for help when you're in trouble, so you're working with anxiety, which is very painful. The person you can talk to is in a different department, and concrete solutions are hard to come by. Broadly speaking, this can be divided into environmental stress and mental stress. First, we'll work on reducing the mental burden while considering more concrete solutions.

dialogue.content: 今後このような形で考えていければと思うのですがいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I'd like to continue approaching it in this way—how does that sound?

dialogue.content: まとめて頂いてありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you for summarizing.

dialogue.content: 本日は時間になってしまいましたが、この窓口は(〇〇〇〇〇〇〇)に開いておりますので、お気軽にご利用ください
dialogue.English: We're out of time for today, but this service is available on (XXXXXXX), so please feel free to use it anytime.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: では本日の相談を終了いたします是非またご利用ください
dialogue.English: Then we'll conclude today's session. Please feel free to use our service again.

dialogue.content: (ありがとうございましたこれでロープレを終了しようと思います本日はありがとうございました)
dialogue.English: (Thank you very much. I think we'll end the role-play here. Thank you for today.)

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.
